question: Why does the tinged aspect not count as the true source of production?
premises: What stands there as the cause of tinging is the object to be willed.
From that part there is no true production.
What arises from it is turbidity and its corresponding form.
inference: Therefore the tinged, object-side aspect yields turbidity, not the primary creative production.
uncertainties: eṣitavyam is read as the object to be willed; the syntax is compressed.
plain_english: What stands there as the cause of tinging is the object to be willed. From that aspect there is no true production; what arises from it is turbidity and its form.
